key_insight: LLM agents can act as a natural-language interface for home energy scheduling and, with function calling, achieve near-optimal appliance control against MILP ground truth.
engineering_relevance: This suggests practical HEMS controllers could reduce electricity costs and improve demand response by translating user preferences into executable optimization constraints.
method: Built a ReAct tool-calling agent for multi-appliance scheduling
Used live Octopus Agile prices, weather forecasts, PV estimates, household usage data, and retrieval-augmented knowledge
Benchmarked GPT-4o-mini, Gemini 2.5 Flash, and Claude Sonnet 4.6 against MILP across tariff, conflict, solar, and week-long scenarios
evidence_signal: Across evaluations, native function calling yielded 100% scheduling success, and week-long agents captured 96.7-98.0% of oracle savings.
watch_item: Performance drops sharply when actions must be text-parsed, so real deployments should rely on robust function-calling and careful constraint handling.
paper_title: LLMs for Agentic Home Energy Management
